outputs: Predictions of whether LLM will generate non-factual responses to fact-seeking questions
Generated factual or non-factual responses to fact-seeking questions

The paper focuses on predicting whether an LLM will generate a non-factual response to a fact-seeking question before generation; the actual generated responses are used only for labeling during training, not as primary NLG outputs under study.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated tasks under 'Other:Fact-Seeking Question Answering'; removed output descriptions that referred to actual generated responses (which are only used for training labels, not as primary NLG outputs); kept models/datasets as they are all relevant NLG components being evaluated
Removed 'PPL' as it is only used as a baseline method for prediction, not as an evaluation metric for generated outputs; AUC is the primary evaluation metric used
No LLM-as-judge evaluation is conducted in this paper; the paper focuses on predicting factuality before generation, not using LLMs to evaluate generated outputs
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper; all evaluations are automated using AUC metric

overall_notes: The paper focuses on predicting non-factuality BEFORE generation occurs, rather than evaluating generated outputs. While it addresses NLG (question answering), the primary contribution is in prediction rather than generation evaluation. The extracted metadata was generally accurate but needed clarification on what constitutes actual NLG outputs vs prediction targets.
